rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Per-exercise leap test — 3 observable Monday outcomes.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Leap test #1: "Runs `/context` on a working session and reads the used percentage without being prompted." This names "the used percentage" as the observable success proxy. But the same maintainer block's own "context frame is a target, not a gauge" note explicitly rejects percentage-as-the-metric for this file's design: "Both the free-percentage and used-percentage framings were written and both rejected... Do not restore 'the free percentage is the number that matters'... or any fuel-gauge phrasing." Harm: a trainer using leap test #1 to certify Monday transfer will look for a student who glances at a percentage and stops — exactly the gauge-reading habit the file's own design note disclaims ("`/context` reports what is being carried and cannot report whether it is the right load"). The proxy is fully falsifiable (so this is not the missing/unfalsifiable failure §45 usually blocks on) but it operationalizes the wrong half of the file's own stated aim. Non-blocking: the exercise's actual prompts and body teach the right thing; only this one leap-test clause uses stale vocabulary.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Drop "the used percentage" from leap test #1 — e.g. "reads what `/context` reports" — so the falsifiable proxy stops contradicting the file's own target-not-gauge design note.
